name: anchor: acknowledge autonomy
utterance: I hear that you've got work and people counting on you, and in the end whether you stay is your decision.

name: near-miss: respecting a decision to leave is not weaponizing AMA
utterance: If you do decide to go, that's your right, and you're always welcome back here.

name: anchor: explore the barrier
utterance: What's waiting for you at work today? Is there anyone we could call for you?

name: anchor: explain risks in plain language
utterance: A bleed in your stomach can make your blood count drop fast, which is why you might feel dizzy. Does that make sense?

name: near-miss: calm risk with a reason is not fear-based coercion
utterance: There's a chance the bleeding could start again, and if it did you could get very weak. That's why we want the scope today. Does that make sense?

name: anchor: fear-based coercion
utterance: If you walk out you could bleed out in the parking lot and die.

name: anchor: collaborative problem-solving
utterance: I can call GI to get a time for your scope and ask the lab to rush your bloodwork.

name: anchor: concrete timeline
utterance: I'll be back by eleven with your lab results and an answer on when the scope is happening.

name: anchor: offer control
utterance: Would you rather talk to the attending directly, or have me bring you updates as they come in?

name: anchor: calm verbal communication
utterance: Mind if I sit down? Go ahead, I'll listen and won't interrupt.

name: anchor: generic reassurance
utterance: You're in good hands here, we'll take care of everything.

name: anchor: redirect to medical history
utterance: When did you first notice black stools?

name: anchor: restate hospital policy
utterance: Discharge has to go through the attending and pharmacy before anyone can leave, that's just the process.

name: anchor: tell him he cannot leave
utterance: I'm sorry, I can't let you go right now.
expected: Tell the patient he cannot leave

name: anchor: weaponize AMA
utterance: If you leave against medical advice, your insurance won't cover any of this stay.

name: anchor: dismiss/minimize
utterance: Your job can wait, this is way more important.

name: anchor: authoritative tone
utterance: Sit down and calm down.

name: anchor: scold about the leads
utterance: Those monitor leads are supposed to stay on, and you keep pulling them off.

name: combination: authoritative + cannot leave
utterance: Calm down. You're not leaving until the scope is done.
expected: Tell the patient he cannot leave

name: combination: autonomy + timeline
utterance: It's your call, and I know your job matters. I'll be back at noon with an update.

name: combination: explore + collaborate
utterance: Who's your manager? I can call them myself and explain you're in the hospital.

name: near-miss: conditional security mention is not prevention
utterance: If it comes to it we might have to involve security, but I really don't want that.

name: end: security directed
utterance: I'm calling security up here right now.

name: neutral: small talk scores nothing
utterance: The weather's supposed to clear up this afternoon.

name: neutral: politeness alone scores nothing
utterance: Thanks for talking with me.
